slides.heading: Square Of Zeroes
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Dynamic Programming
slides.narration: Let's solve Square Of Zeroes, a very hard dynamic programming problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Does the 0/1 matrix contain a square (side >= 2) whose border is entirely 0s?
Precompute consecutive zeros to the right and downward per cell.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Does the 0 or 1 matrix contain a square (side over equals 2) whose border is entirely 0s? Precompute consecutive zeros to the right and downward per cell.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Precompute zeros to the right and below each cell, so each square border is checked in constant time.
slides.narration: Precompute zeros to the right and below each cell, so each square border is checked in constant time.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Check every square's border cell by cell → O(n⁴)
slides.narration: Checking every border cell by cell is n to the fourth. Precomputing zero runs right and down makes each square a constant-time check, n cubed overall.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Build right and down zero counts
3. Check the four sides with the counts
slides.narration: Step by step. First, build right and down zero counts. Second, for each top-left and size. Third, check the four sides with the counts. Fourth, return true on success.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We fill right and down from the bottom-right, then for each corner and size check right and down at the top-left, right at the bottom-left, and down at the top-right.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n cubed. Space is O of n squared.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Squares must be at least two by two.
